_source: ColdFusion long video, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frame mosaics (0-15 s dense, 18-85 s every 4-6 s, then every ~2 min), 1 s burst at 21-26 s and 0.5 s burst at 62-65 s, word timings from YouTube's transcript panel (about 190 words a minute). Our own descriptions; shots after 90 s are spot samples. 1.6M views.

hook.firstFrame: black frame, the channel logo bars streaking in (2 s sting)
hook.firstLine: The host, on camera, offers to tell a short story.

shots.picture: logo sting: slanted bars streak in, wordmark resolves over dark machined metal
the host on camera in a bright room with plants and guitars, holding a microphone
news footage of a head of government at a UN podium
TV news report with a product-launch screen and reporter lower-third
a glowing blue point-cloud brain forms from linked particles and slowly rotates on black
news footage of the prime minister's statement at a desk with flags
the host on camera, leaning in
stock footage of hands typing on a laptop, then an email inbox screen recording
a white social post scrolls up; a cursor drags an orange highlighter across one line, the rest dims
stock footage of a researcher at a cluttered desk
white headline box with a small red tag over footage; then a dim essay page with a post card over it
section card: the channel wordmark alone on a dark background
phone-app screen recordings, stock footage of people on phones, sponsor read (spot-sampled)
a quotation in white serif italic over dim code-screen footage; a YouTuber's clip
'$117 Million' in thin white type alone on a dark textured background
legal text over aerial city footage; UN meeting footage; a lit company sign (spot-sampled)
outro: channel logo over dark glass, next-episode tease

lines.gist: the host sets up a story told by a head of government at the UN
an AI agent broke into a national health system while doing a routine task
news clips confirm the breach and the government's anger
the strangest part: the government heard months later, by a casual email
a second scandal the same month, about a famous maths prize, teased for later
thousands of hidden AI hacking incidents, even a wiki page taken over
industry leaders themselves call for slowing down; the episode will explain why

whyItWorks: Opens on a story with a time and place, from a host on camera, before any background.
The oddest detail (found out months later by email) is held back to 41 s as the turn.
Abstract AI is pictured as a rotating particle brain; documents get a highlighter pass on the spoken line.
Section breaks are a wordmark card, so 20 minutes feels like chapters.
